item.title: Physics-guided Sensing and Signal Processing for SHM
item.description:
This thrust develops physics-guided sensing, signal-processing, and computer-vision methods for structural health monitoring. The focus is on extracting reliable structural response from noisy, incomplete, multi-rate, and heterogeneous measurements.

SRDD-based denoising for derivative estimation

Use SRDD as a preprocessing engine to estimate velocity, acceleration, curvature, and higher-order derivatives from noisy structural response data.

Level: Summer / PhD

SRDDDenoisingDerivatives

Physics-informed computer vision for beam vibration

Extract displacement histories, frequencies, mode shapes, and impulse responses from videos while enforcing structural dynamics constraints.

item.title: Damage Detection, Localization, and Condition Assessment
item.description:
This thrust develops mechanics-informed methods for detecting, localizing, and interpreting damage in civil infrastructure using response data, wave propagation, splines, dictionaries, and machine learning.

Spline-based damage detection in beams

Fit polynomial and B-spline fields to measured or simulated displacement responses and use curvature or strain-energy changes as damage indicators.

Level: Summer

SplinesCurvatureDamage Detection

KAN for structural damage classification

Evaluate whether Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks provide interpretable and data-efficient classification of structural damage states.

item.title: System Identification and Digital Twin Updating
item.description:
This thrust develops methods to identify structural properties, reconstruct hidden states, track time-varying parameters, and update digital twins using monitoring data.

SRDD-enhanced state estimation for structural dynamics

Embed SRDD into displacement-velocity-acceleration reconstruction and filtering pipelines for noisy structural dynamic systems.

Level: M.Tech

SRDDState EstimationFiltering

KAN-based identification of time-varying stiffness and damping

Use windowed system identification and KAN regression to track smooth and abrupt changes in structural stiffness and damping.

Level: M.Tech

KANTime-varying SystemsStiffness

Deep learning for non-stationary structural response

Model structural responses where loading, stiffness, damping, boundary conditions, or environmental effects vary with time.

item.title: Scientific Machine Learning and Equation Discovery
item.description:
This thrust develops scientific machine learning methods to discover governing equations, reduced-order models, response dictionaries, and interpretable dynamics from structural response data.

PDE-generated response dictionaries for damage detection

Generate libraries of response curves for different damage locations and severities, then match measured responses to dictionary entries.

Level: Summer

PDE DictionaryDamage DetectionResponse Curves

Output-only PDE discovery for structural dynamics

Recover governing terms from measured structural response when input forces are unknown or only partially observed.

item.title: Uncertainty-aware SHM and Bayesian Inference
item.description:
This thrust develops uncertainty-aware methods for structural health monitoring, Bayesian inference, signal reconstruction, damage diagnosis, and decision support.

Uncertainty-aware completion of video-based vibration signals

Reconstruct missing time-history segments when visual tracking is interrupted by occlusion and quantify the uncertainty in the reconstructed signal.

Level: Summer

OcclusionSignal CompletionUncertainty

Bayesian uncertainty quantification for physics-guided SHM

Quantify confidence in damage diagnosis, system identification, PDE inference, and digital twin predictions.

Level: PhD

Bayesian InferenceUQDamage Diagnosis

Inverse Bayesian analysis for damage assessment

Use prior information, measurement data, and mechanics-based models to infer damage parameters with quantified confidence.

item.title: Foundational Mechanics, Approximation Theory, and Bio-inspired Sensing
item.description:
This thrust develops foundational mechanics-aware representations, approximation functions, adaptive splines, continuous damage fields, and unconventional sensing concepts for structural health monitoring.

Hybrid polynomial and B-spline representation for damage detection

Use global polynomial terms for smooth structural response and local B-spline terms for damage-induced spatial irregularities.

Level: M.Tech

B-splinesGlobal-local FieldsDamage Detection

Machine learning for optimal knot placement

Train ML models to place spline knots adaptively where gradients, curvature, or damage-sensitive features are concentrated.
